home-remodeling.local_heading: Why Aventura remodels need a different playbook
intro_paragraphs: Aventura is mostly a vertical city. The towers came up in waves — Turnberry and Mystic Pointe from the late seventies through the nineties, Porto Vita and The Point in the two-thousands, Echo and Privé at Island Estates more recently — and inside many of them, the units still wear their original dropped soffits, choppy galley kitchens, and beige tile. Owners here gut those floor plans and start over. In the two single-family pockets, Aventura Lakes and Country Club Estates along the Turnberry fairways, the work is different: taking late-nineties builder houses to the standard the address implies.

Every remodel in the city runs through the City of Aventura Community Development Department, whose Building Division permits and inspects everything from flooring to full guts — yes, flooring needs a permit here. In the towers, the city is only half the approval: associations want insurance certificates, contractor registration, service-elevator reservations, and defined work hours before a hammer swings. Many older buildings are also in the middle of milestone inspections and structural reserve studies, so we sequence unit work around building-wide projects. Impact windows and doors need Miami-Dade product approvals, because this is High-Velocity Hurricane Zone territory.

Two decades and change in South Florida, 150-plus remodels and additions delivered, and not one of them unpermitted: that is the PGX record. In Aventura that means a fixed written scope before demolition, a supervisor on site daily, and corridors, lobbies, and elevators protected as carefully as your new stone. One team carries the project from estimate through warranty, and your association's property manager gets answers before they have to ask. Licensed and insured, Lic. CGC1539072.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to remodel a condo in Aventura?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of Aventura requires permits for kitchen and bathroom remodels, flooring, window and door replacement, and most alterations — the Building Division reviews plans and inspects the work. Your association will have its own approval package on top of that, usually insurance certificates, contractor registration, and deposits. We prepare both submissions, track the city permit through its eTRAKiT portal, and schedule inspections so the project never stalls between the two.

faqs.q: How do milestone inspections affect remodeling in my building?
faqs.a: Florida now requires milestone structural inspections for condo buildings three stories and up — generally at 30 years, and as early as 25 where local officials require it for coastal buildings — then every ten years, along with structural integrity reserve studies. Practically, that means many Aventura towers have engineering assessments or concrete work underway or scheduled. We check what your building has planned before committing dates, so your finished remodel is not interrupted by a facade project six months later.

faqs.q: How long does a whole-home remodel take in Aventura?
faqs.a: Be realistic: association review can add weeks before the city even sees your plans, and a full-gut renovation then runs several months of construction depending on scope and finish lead times. Simple interior permits generally move faster than structural ones. What we control is the schedule we commit to — a written timeline tied to a fixed scope, with long-lead materials ordered before demolition so the project never sits idle waiting on a slab of stone.

faqs.q: Can you work within my building's rules?
faqs.a: That is most of the job in this city. We register with your association, carry the required insurance certificates, book the service elevator, protect corridors and lobbies, and keep noisy work inside the permitted hours. Our supervisors deal directly with building management and security, so issues get resolved at the loading dock instead of at a board meeting. Buildings remember contractors — we make sure they remember us for the right reasons.

faqs.q: How much should I expect to spend remodeling an Aventura home?
faqs.a: It depends on scope and finish level more than square footage — custom cabinetry, stone, and full MEP replacement drive the number far more than paint does. We will not pretend there is a meaningful per-foot figure before seeing the unit. PGX is a high-end contractor, not the cheap bid: you get a fixed written proposal with the real number up front, and that number does not drift once demolition starts.

kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: Kitchen craft from Williams Island to Aventura Lakes
intro_paragraphs: Most Aventura kitchens were drawn when nobody expected to look at them: galley layouts tucked behind a wall in Mystic Pointe and Turnberry-era units, builder-grade runs in late-nineties Aventura Lakes houses, formal but dated rooms in Country Club Estates. Today's owners want the opposite — the wall gone, an island with seating, stone with some movement to it, and lighting that was designed rather than inherited. On Williams Island and at Porto Vita, we regularly take a three-decade-old kitchen down to the slab and give the residence the open plan it should have had all along.

Kitchen remodels here are permitted work — the City of Aventura Community Development Department lists kitchen remodeling among the projects that require a permit, and its Building Division inspects the electrical, plumbing, and mechanical behind your new cabinetry. In a tower, plumbing and vent routes are governed by riser stacks and concrete slabs, so relocating a sink or moving appliances takes planning, not optimism. Most buildings are all-electric, which is why induction has quietly conquered Aventura's high-rise kitchens. Associations add their own layer: insurance certificates, elevator bookings for slab-sized deliveries, and set working hours.

The kitchens other contractors photograph are the kind PGX actually delivers: custom cabinetry measured to the millimeter, stone templated after the boxes are set, appliances that sit flush because someone checked the specs twice. You get a fixed written scope before demolition and a supervisor on site every day — not a subcontractor with your key. After 20-plus years and more than 150 remodels and additions across South Florida, we know exactly which details fail first, and we build those parts twice as carefully.

faqs.q: Can I open my condo kitchen to the living room?
faqs.a: Often, yes — many kitchen walls in Aventura towers are non-structural partitions. But we verify against the building's drawings, and bring in an engineer when anything is ambiguous, before a design gets drawn around an assumption. Your association will want plans and formal sign-off, and the city permits the demolition plus any electrical and plumbing changes that follow. When the wall can come down, the difference in light alone usually settles the question.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a kitchen remodel in Aventura?
faqs.a: Yes — kitchen remodels are specifically on the City of Aventura's list of work requiring a permit, along with the flooring, electrical, and plumbing changes that come with them. The Building Division reviews the plans and inspects the rough work before it disappears behind cabinetry. Unpermitted kitchens surface at resale and in association records, so doing it right the first time is cheaper than doing it twice. We handle the full submission and inspection schedule.

faqs.q: Can I have a gas range in an Aventura high-rise?
faqs.a: Usually not — most towers in the city are all-electric, and adding gas service to a high-rise unit is rarely feasible. The good news is that high-end induction has closed the gap: faster than gas, easier to clean, and better suited to a sealed, air-conditioned residence anyway. In Aventura Lakes and Country Club Estates houses, gas is a real option, permitted and installed properly if the range you love demands a flame.

faqs.q: How long will my kitchen be out of commission?
faqs.a: The honest answer: custom cabinetry lead time drives the calendar more than construction does. We order cabinets, appliances, and stone before demolition day, so the kitchen is torn out for the build, not for the wait. Add association approval and city permitting to the front end and a typical high-end kitchen runs a few months door to door — a schedule we put in writing, alongside the scope, before we start.

faqs.q: What does a high-end kitchen remodel cost in Aventura?
faqs.a: The range is wide because the drivers are choices, not mysteries: fully custom cabinetry versus semi-custom, exotic stone versus quartz, and the appliance package — which can quietly rival the cabinetry budget. We build at the level Aventura's better residences expect, so we are rarely the lowest bid, and we are fine with that. What you get instead is a fixed written number that survives contact with construction.

bathroom-remodeling.local_heading: Waterproofing matters more twelve floors up
intro_paragraphs: The bathrooms in Aventura's eighties and nineties towers — Mystic Pointe, the early Turnberry buildings, the Williams Island originals — were generous for their day and dated for ours: cultured marble, gold-toned shower frames, soffits concealing who knows what. Owners now rebuild them as true primary suites, with curbless showers, freestanding tubs, book-matched stone, and warm layered light. Over in Aventura Lakes and Country Club Estates, the ambition is the same but the square footage is friendlier, and the plumbing does not run through a neighbor's ceiling. Either way, this is the room where Aventura owners spend most seriously per square foot.

Bathroom remodeling is permitted work in this city — the City of Aventura Building Division reviews the plumbing, electrical, and structural details, then inspects the stages you cannot see afterward, which are precisely the stages that matter. In a high-rise, your shower pan sits over someone's ceiling, so we flood-test pans, document the membrane, and photograph everything before tile goes down. Drain relocations are governed by the slab and the building's riser stacks, meaning we confirm feasibility on paper before you fall in love with a floor plan. Associations typically want plans, insurance certificates, and scheduled work hours as well.

PGX treats the waterproofing as the actual product and the marble as the reward. Fixed written scope, daily supervision, licensed trades, and the sequence done in order: membrane, flood test, inspection, then stone. We protect corridors and elevators on the way in, keep dust behind sealed barriers, and leave your property manager with nothing to write us about. Twenty-plus years in South Florida have taught us exactly which shortcuts leak, and we decline all of them.

faqs.q: How do you protect the unit below mine during a bathroom remodel?
faqs.a: Wet rooms are where high-rise remodels go wrong, so this is where our process is strictest: water shut-off coordination with building engineering, sealed containment during demolition, new waterproofing membranes flood-tested and photographed before tile, and city inspections passed at each hidden stage. We carry the insurance your association requires and document everything, because the best conversation with a downstairs neighbor is the one that never needs to happen.

faqs.q: Do bathroom remodels need permits in Aventura?
faqs.a: Yes — bathroom remodeling appears explicitly on the City of Aventura's permit-required list, and for good reason: the important work is plumbing, electrical, and waterproofing that gets buried behind tile. The Building Division inspects those stages before they are covered. In a condo, add your association's approval package to the sequence. We manage both tracks in parallel so the approvals overlap instead of stacking end to end.

faqs.q: Can I move my toilet or shower in a condo bathroom?
faqs.a: Sometimes — it depends on how far the fixture must travel from the building's riser stacks and what the slab allows. Some Aventura buildings offer more flexibility than others, and the answer lives in the structural drawings, not in a hunch. We investigate before design begins, so the layout you approve is one that can actually be built. When relocation is off the table, a well-planned layout usually recovers what the plumbing will not give.

faqs.q: How long does a bathroom remodel take in Aventura?
faqs.a: Association review and city permitting occupy the front weeks; construction itself depends on scope, and stone or glass lead times can add more. A full primary-suite rebuild typically spans a few months from approval to final inspection. We compress what can be compressed — materials ordered early, trades scheduled tightly, inspections booked ahead — and we give you the schedule in writing rather than as a feeling.

faqs.q: What does a primary bathroom remodel cost here?
faqs.a: Stone, glass, and fixtures set the ceiling; layout changes and plumbing relocation set the floor. A high-end primary bath in an Aventura tower or Country Club Estates home is a serious investment, and we would rather show you a fixed written number after a walk-through than recite a range that means nothing. What we can promise up front: the price includes the waterproofing done right, which is the part you should refuse to economize on.

home-additions.local_heading: Room to grow in a condo town
intro_paragraphs: Single-family homes are the exception in Aventura — the gated streets of Aventura Lakes and the small golf-course enclave of Country Club Estates — so owners who outgrow one rarely find another around the corner. They extend instead: a rear addition off the kitchen, a second story where the lot cannot spread sideways, a garage rebuilt for family who visit and never quite leave. The towers have their own version of an addition — buying the unit next door and combining two residences into one — and in Aventura's condo market, that move is often the smartest square footage available.

An addition here is a full permitting exercise with the City of Aventura Community Development Department: zoning review for setbacks and lot coverage, structural plans for foundations and tie beams, and inspections at every stage. Aventura Lakes and Country Club Estates both layer homeowner-association review on top, so elevations and materials get approved before the city weighs in. Unit combinations run a different gauntlet — association consent, engineering review of the shared wall, and permits for the structural opening and the rejoined systems. Everything exterior must meet High-Velocity Hurricane Zone wind loads, and near the water, flood-zone rules can shape what happens at ground level.

PGX has delivered more than 150 remodels and additions over 20-plus years in South Florida, and additions are where that record earns its keep: foundations, tie-beam upgrades, and roof tie-ins are not the place for a contractor's first attempt. You get a fixed written scope, engineering coordinated under one roof, daily site supervision, and a realistic plan for living in the house while we build onto it. When it is finished, the new space should read as original — not as an afterthought with better insulation.

faqs.q: Can I add a second story to my Aventura Lakes home?
faqs.a: Frequently, yes — subject to what the existing foundation can carry and what your HOA and the city's zoning rules allow for height and coverage. The sequence matters: structural evaluation first, then HOA architectural review, then permitting with the City of Aventura. We coordinate the engineering and shepherd both approvals, so by the time construction starts, every question about loads, setbacks, and elevations has already been answered on paper.

faqs.q: Can two condo units really be combined into one?
faqs.a: Yes, and it happens in Aventura's towers more than people realize. The requirements are real: your association must approve, an engineer must review the shared wall before any opening is cut, and the city permits the structural work plus the electrical, plumbing, and HVAC systems being merged. Done properly, the result is a single residence with no seams — done casually, it is a problem at resale. We only do it the first way.

faqs.q: Do flood zones affect additions in Aventura?
faqs.a: They can. Parcels near the Intracoastal and the lakes may sit in mapped FEMA flood zones, where federal substantial-improvement rules can influence how much you invest in an existing structure and how new ground-level space must be built. It is not a reason to abandon an addition — it is a reason to check the property's zone and run the numbers early, which we do before design money gets spent.

faqs.q: How long does a home addition take here?
faqs.a: Longer than a remodel, honestly. Design and engineering come first, then HOA review, then city plan review — months of paper before ground is broken — followed by several months of construction depending on size and complexity. We front-load the approvals, order structural materials early, and phase the work so your household keeps functioning. The schedule you get from us is written, dated, and built to be kept.

faqs.q: Is an addition worth it compared to moving?
faqs.a: In most markets that is a close call. In Aventura, where single-family inventory is thin and the alternative is usually leaving the city, extending a house you already like is often the rational move — you keep the street, the schools, and the commute, and put the transaction costs into construction instead. We are happy to walk the house and tell you plainly whether the structure and the lot support what you have in mind.

outdoor-living.local_heading: Built for golf views and waterfront weather
intro_paragraphs: Aventura was designed around being outside — the three-mile exercise trail circling the Turnberry golf course sees more daily traffic than some gyms — and private outdoor space here is catching up to the public kind. Country Club Estates owners are turning golf-course backyards into covered outdoor rooms with summer kitchens; Aventura Lakes families want pergolas, pavers, and lake-facing terraces that handle both birthday parties and August. Even tower residents invest at the threshold, upgrading terrace finishes, railings, and outdoor spaces to the limit of what the association and the wind engineer will allow.

Exterior work in Aventura answers to two authorities. The City of Aventura Building Division permits and inspects structures, driveways, and window or door replacement — and in a High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, pergolas, screen enclosures, and every impact opening need product approvals and engineering to match. Then come the associations: Aventura Lakes and Country Club Estates review exterior materials and colors, while condo associations control nearly everything beyond your terrace door. Add the salt-heavy air drifting off the Intracoastal, which quietly destroys bargain hardware, and material selection becomes the difference between a terrace that lasts and one you rebuild.

PGX approaches exterior work the way we approach interiors: fixed written scope, engineering before enthusiasm, daily supervision, and finishes chosen for the climate rather than the catalog. We coordinate re-roofs with painters and sequence stucco around window replacement so nothing gets built twice, and we specify marine-grade fasteners because we have seen what five summers do to the other kind. In gated communities we keep crews tidy, schedules honest, and neighbors unbothered — the review board hears about the results, not the process.

faqs.q: Can I build a summer kitchen at my Aventura home?
faqs.a: In Aventura Lakes or Country Club Estates, yes — with city permits for the gas, plumbing, and electrical runs, and your HOA's blessing on the design. On tower terraces the story is different: fire codes and most associations restrict open-flame grills on balconies, so the options narrow to electric equipment and whatever your building's rules allow. We will tell you which side of that line your project sits on before anyone gets attached to a rendering.

faqs.q: Do pergolas and pavers need permits in Aventura?
faqs.a: Pergolas and other structures do — and in a High-Velocity Hurricane Zone they also need engineering and anchoring designed for serious wind, not just a bag of concrete per post. Driveways and most hardscape changes go through city review as well, and your HOA will want drawings of anything visible from the street. It sounds like a lot of paperwork because it is; we handle all of it as part of the scope.

faqs.q: What outdoor materials hold up near the Intracoastal?
faqs.a: The salt air is patient and undefeated, so we specify accordingly: 316 stainless steel or marine-grade hardware, powder-coated aluminum over raw steel, porcelain pavers that ignore moisture, dense stone sealed properly, and cabinetry built for exterior life rather than adapted to it. The cost difference over builder-grade materials is real but modest — far smaller than the cost of replacing a corroded outdoor kitchen in year six.

faqs.q: Can you coordinate a re-roof with other exterior work?
faqs.a: Yes, and you should insist on it. Roofing, stucco repair, painting, and window replacement all touch the same edges of the building, and the order of operations determines whether the flashing, waterproofing, and finishes actually work together. We sequence the trades under one schedule and one contract, so the roofer is not blaming the painter while your ceiling stain grows. One accountable builder, one warranty conversation.

faqs.q: How does hurricane season affect outdoor projects in Aventura?
faqs.a: It shapes the schedule more than it stops the work. We plan concrete, roofing, and structural phases with the season in mind, keep sites secured and materials strapped when weather threatens, and never leave your property exposed going into a storm week. The upside of building in a High-Velocity Hurricane Zone is that everything we install — pergolas, openings, roofing — is engineered for exactly the weather everyone worries about.
